Good morning! Here is your daily brief for today.

First, Azure updates. In infrastructure, the AKS team announced the deprecation of Availability Sets. Any clusters still using virtual machine availability sets will be automatically migrated to virtual machines on September thirtieth. The same release also introduced a general availability of Azure Ephemeral OS Disk with full caching, which stores the entire operating system locally and reduces remote‑storage reads for both virtual machines and virtual machine scale sets. Dell’s Managed PowerScale service is now generally available on Azure, offering high‑performance, file‑system‑based storage for large unstructured data workloads. Additionally, user‑bound user‑delegation SAS for Azure Storage is now generally available, tying shared access signatures to Entra ID identities for tighter credential control.

On the security side, Microsoft published a Threat Matrix that aligns with the MITRE ATT&CK framework to help prioritize and mitigate risks across cloud web applications and serverless services. A recent advisory warned about a passkey‑themed social engineering campaign that exploits MFA persistence and Microsoft Graph to harvest data from SharePoint, OneDrive and email. A critical zero‑day vulnerability dubbed ShieldCrash has been identified in Windows Defender and requires immediate patching. Finally, the restriction of user‑delegation SAS to Entra ID identities has been reinforced to eliminate reliance on storage account keys.

In cloud and DevOps news, a new Manifest Facade Pattern is available for Azure DevOps pipelines, helping teams curb parameter sprawl in shared templates. A recent study found that one in five Managed Cloud Platform access policies are broken or missing, highlighting ongoing compliance challenges. The Azure Developer CLI extension framework is now generally available, enabling custom CLI extensions for development workflows. And Playwright Workspaces have reached general availability in Azure regions East US, Japan East and Switzerland North, providing managed browsers for large‑scale end‑to‑end testing.

Moving on to AI news today, there are no major announcements to report.

Finally, in market coverage, there are no notable movements to highlight at this time.

Bottom line: Azure is delivering several important general availability features and critical security updates, while AI and market headlines are quiet today. That is your update. Have a great day!
